class.name: NetwPropertyConfig
class.brief_description: Declares how a script variable is replicated, reached by [method Netw.configure_property].
class.description:
Mark a property with [method state], [method input] or [method broadcast], and every change to it is sent each tick. There is no send call to make. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").state().quantize(pos_q) Netw.configure_property(self, &"move_dir").input() Netw.configure_property(self, &"aim_dir").broadcast()
func _physics_process(_dt: float) -> void: move_dir = Input.get_vector("left", "right", "up", "down") aim_dir = (get_global_mouse_position() - position).normalized() # the next tick sends every changed property [/codeblock] [enum NetwPropertySet.Record] compares the three kinds. A property with none of them is sent only when [method Netw.sync_property] is called. [method volatile], [method retained], [method epsilon] and [method persisted] apply to one property. [method every_tick], [method on_change], [method heartbeat], [method windowed], [method audience] and [method masked] apply to every property of the same kind on the script, so the last call wins. [b]Rigid bodies[/b] When the entity root is a [RigidBody3D] or a [RigidBody2D], [code]position[/code], [code]quaternion[/code] ([code]rotation[/code] in 2D), [code]linear_velocity[/code], [code]angular_velocity[/code] and [code]sleeping[/code] read and write the body's physics state. [code]position[/code] stays relative to the parent. While [member RigidBody3D.freeze] is on, position and rotation use the node transform. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").state() Netw.configure_property(self, &"quaternion").state() Netw.configure_property(self, &"linear_velocity").state() [/codeblock] [b]Note:[/b] a [NetwMemberConfig] method such as [method NetwMemberConfig.call_local] returns a [NetwMemberConfig], so call the methods of this class first in a chain.

method.name: audience
method.description: Sends properties of this kind to the server only, or to every peer when [param server_only] is [code]false[/code]. Sets [member NetwPropertySet.audience]. [method input] already sends to the server only.

method.name: broadcast
method.description:
The controlling peer owns the value and every peer sees it, with no server check. Use it for cosmetic values such as an aim direction. The server keeps no history of it. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_property(self, &"aim_dir").broadcast()
func _process(_dt: float) -> void: aim_dir = (get_global_mouse_position() - position).normalized() # every other peer's copy of this node follows [/codeblock] Add [method masked] when many peers watch the same entity.

method.name: carry_along
method.description: When a correction restores this value, advances it to the present using the rate in [param channel]. Without it, the value is restored as the server had it a few ticks ago. [codeblock] # the body integrates position from velocity, so a restore advances along it Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").state().carry_along(&"velocity") [/codeblock] [param channel] must be another [method state] property of the same entity. Use [method carry_step] instead when the rate changes quickly. Declaring both on one property is an error, and neither is used.

method.name: carry_step
method.description:
When a correction restores this value, advances it to the present by calling [param step] once for each tick the server has not acknowledged yet. Use it for a value only your code changes. A value the physics engine also changes cannot be advanced this way, and the rule is disabled. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_property(self, &"spin").state().carry_step(_carry_spin)
func _carry_spin(value: Vector3, ctx: NetwPredictCarryContext) -> Vector3: return value + _drive_axis(ctx.state) * ctx.state[&"speed"] * ctx.delta [/codeblock] [param step] must be a method or lambda of a [Node], may read only its [NetwPredictCarryContext], and must not write anything. A result that does not reproduce the recorded ticks is rejected, and the value is restored as the server had it. Declaring both this and [method carry_along] on one property is an error, and neither is used. [method NetwPredictionHandle.reachability] reports whether the rule is in use.

method.name: causal
method.description: Marks the value as one the next step reads, so it is compared and corrected. This is the default. [codeblock] Netw.configure_property(self, &"velocity").state().causal() [/codeblock]

method.name: converge
method.description: Moves the value part of the way toward the server's value during a correction, by [param stiffness], instead of writing it outright. [code]0.0[/code] writes it outright. A value with no midpoint, such as a [bool], is always written outright. [codeblock] Netw.configure_property(self, &"heading").state().causal().converge(0.4) [/codeblock]

method.name: cosmetic
method.description: Marks the value as display only, so a difference in it never causes a correction. A correction still writes it. [codeblock] Netw.configure_property(self, &"skid_intensity").state().cosmetic() [/codeblock]

method.name: derived
method.description: Marks the value as one the body recomputes each step from other properties, so a difference in it never causes a correction. A correction still writes it. [codeblock] # recomputed from velocity every tick Netw.configure_property(self, &"speed").state().derived() [/codeblock]

method.name: epsilon
method.description: How far this value may drift from the server's before it is corrected, in its own units. Without it, the value uses [member NetwPredictionHandle.divergence_epsilon]. [code]0.0[/code] corrects any error. [codeblock] Netw.configure_property(self, &"velocity").state().epsilon(0.05) [/codeblock] Use [method reconcile_only] for a value that should never cause a correction.

method.name: every_tick
method.description: Sends properties of this kind every tick even when nothing changed, at most once per [param interval] seconds. [codeblock] # position changes every tick anyway Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").state().every_tick() [/codeblock]

method.name: heartbeat
method.description: Re-sends properties of this kind every [param ticks] ticks even when nothing changed, so a peer that missed a change catches up. [method input] properties ignore it. [codeblock] # a lost "stunned" change heals within a second at 60 ticks Netw.configure_property(self, &"stunned").state().heartbeat(60) [/codeblock]

method.name: input
method.description:
The controlling peer owns the value and only the server sees it. Use it for player input. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_property(self, &"move_dir").input()
func _physics_process(dt: float) -> void: if entity.is_controlled_locally: move_dir = Input.get_vector("left", "right", "up", "down") # both peers run this, the client predicts and the server decides velocity = move_dir * SPEED [/codeblock] Each send also carries the last two ticks of input, so a lost packet is recovered from the next one. [method windowed] changes how many. Correction settings such as [method carry_along] are ignored on an input.

method.name: masked
method.description: Sends each peer only the properties that changed since it last confirmed, which saves bandwidth when many peers watch one entity. [codeblock] # 50 spectators, each gets only what changed for them Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").broadcast().masked() [/codeblock]

method.name: on_change
method.description: Sends properties of this kind only when one changed. This is the default.

method.name: on_spawn
method.description: Sends the value with the spawn, and sets it on every peer before the node enters the tree, so [method Node._enter_tree] and [method Node._ready] can read it. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_property(self, &"pet_name").on_spawn() [/codeblock]

method.name: persisted
method.description:
Saves the server's value of this property into [param column] of the entity's saved row, whether or not it is also replicated. [param column] must come from the [NetwSchema] given to [method NetwPersistenceConfig.schema] and match the property's type. [codeblock] var schema := game.save_schema
# never replicated, the server still saves it Netw.configure_property(self, &"gold").persisted(schema.column_ref(0))
# replicated and saved Netw.configure_property(self, &"position") \ .state().persisted(schema.column_ref(1))
# sent by the client, saved by the server Netw.configure_property(self, &"loadout") \ .input().persisted(schema.column_ref(2)) [/codeblock] How often the row is saved is set with [method NetwPersistenceConfig.interval].

method.name: reconcile_only
method.description: A difference in this value never causes a correction, but a correction caused by another value still restores it. [codeblock] Netw.configure_property(self, &"heading").state().reconcile_only() [/codeblock]

method.name: retained
method.description: Sends changes reliably. Use it for a value that changes rarely and must not be missed. It cannot be used on the state of a predicted entity. [codeblock] # a lost "stunned = true" would never be corrected Netw.configure_property(self, &"stunned").state().retained() [/codeblock]

method.name: state
method.description:
The server owns the value, every peer sees it, and lag compensation can rewind it. A client predicting this entity is corrected against it, within [method epsilon]. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").state().quantize(pos_q)
func _physics_process(dt: float) -> void: position += velocity * dt # on the server that is enough, every client's copy follows [/codeblock]

method.name: teleport_at
method.description: How large this value's error may be before a correction teleports the body, in its own units. Without it, the value uses [member NetwPredictionHandle.teleport_threshold]. [code]0.0[/code] teleports on every correction this value causes. [codeblock] Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").state() \ .carry_along(&"velocity").teleport_at(3.0) # metres Netw.configure_property(self, &"heading").state() \ .carry_along(&"angular_speed").teleport_at(1.0) # radians [/codeblock]

method.name: teleport_only
method.description: Only a teleport writes this value, and an ordinary correction leaves it alone. Pair it with [method carry_along] or [method carry_step] so the teleport restores it at the present, or with [method reconcile_only] so it never causes a correction. [codeblock] Netw.configure_property(self, &"angular_velocity").state().teleport_only() [/codeblock]

method.name: volatile
method.description: Sends changes unreliably, and only the newest value counts. Use it for a value that changes every tick. This is the default.

method.name: windowed
method.description: Each send also carries the last [param samples] ticks of values, so a lost packet is recovered from the next one. [codeblock] # input() sends 2, and 3 survives two lost packets in a row Netw.configure_property(self, &"motion").input().windowed(3) [/codeblock]

members.member: Set by [method epsilon]. A negative value uses [member NetwPredictionHandle.divergence_epsilon].
Always [code]true[/code]. Tells this class apart from a [NetwMemberConfig] for an RPC or a signal.
Whether changes are sent unreliably or reliably. Set by [method volatile] and [method retained].
Whether a difference in the value causes a correction. Set by [method causal], [method derived] and [method cosmetic].
Set by [method every_tick]. Negative when unset.
Set by [method every_tick] and [method on_change], or [constant UNSET].
Set by [method teleport_at]. A negative value uses [member NetwPredictionHandle.teleport_threshold].

constants.constant: A setting no call has written yet.
